test_title: PYST 29: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I - Mathematics (Held On: 17 Jun, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: maths
question: Two taps can fill a cistern in 3 hours and 57 hours, respectively. A third tap can empty it in 3 hours. How long (in hours) will it take to fill one-third of the empty cistern, if all of them are opened together?
solution:
**Given:**

Tap A fills in 3 hours

Tap B fills in 57 hours

Tap C empties in 3 hours

**Calculations:**

⇒ LCM(3, 57, 3) = 57 (total capacity = 57 units)

⇒ Efficiency A = 57 ÷ 3 = 19 units/hr

⇒ Efficiency B = 57 ÷ 57 = 1 unit/hr

⇒ Efficiency C (empty) = 57 ÷ 3 = 19 units/hr

⇒ Net efficiency = 19 + 1 − 19 = 1 unit/hr

⇒ Work required = 1/3 of cistern = 57 ÷ 3 = 19 units

⇒ Time = 19 ÷ 1 = 19 hours

**∴ Time taken = 19 hours.**
